newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Weak NZ job advertising manifest in June - ANZ.
newsitem.headline: Weak NZ job advertising manifest in June - ANZ.

text.p: The trend number of New Zealand job ads fell by 1.5 percent in June following a 0.2 percent drop in May, ANZ Bank said on Tuesday.
In annual terms, the trend number of job ads was down 4.5 percent.

"The continued decline in the number of positions advertised in Wellington and Christchurch, and more recently in Auckland, is suggestive of some further weakness in the labour market over the June 1997 quarter," ANZ said.
Job ads fell in all three main centres during June, with Auckland's advertising fall following on several months of weak but sustained growth.
The monthly trend in Auckland job ads dropped 1.1 percent in June, following small rises since October. The trend number of ads was 1.3 percent lower than in June 1996.
Job ads in Wellington fell 0.7 percent in June, with 13.6 percent fewer jobs advertised in the capital than a year ago.
Job advertising in Christchurch recorded a steep 4.5 percent drop in June. In annual terms, the trend number of job ads was 14.3 percent lower than in June 1996.
